quarterly_data.quarter: Novo Nordisk press release: People switching from weight-loss injections to Novo's (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company real-world study OCTANE (de-identified data from the Ro telehealth platform, the first analysis of a Ro-Novo collaboration), presented at EASD 2026: 194 adults with overweight or obesity who switched from injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide to the once-daily Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide) and stayed on treatment lost an average of 4.1% of body weight (4.0 kg / 8.8 lb) after three months (p<0.001); 40.7% achieved 5% or more weight loss and the share with BMI of 30 or more fell from 87.1% to 65.5% (21.6 percentage points); 82.4% of those with data reported at least one treatment improvement. The company notes real-world studies evaluate associations and cannot determine causality, and that persistence was required (possible selection bias) and weights were self-reported. The release states the Wegovy pill is launched in the US, United Arab Emirates, UK and Germany, with launches in select markets in the coming quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: 4.1% (4.0 kg) average weight loss at three months; 40.7% achieved 5% or more; obesity share 87.1% to 65.5%; 194 patients; Wegovy pill launched in US, UAE, UK and Germany
